'''Christopher John Lamb''' {{post-nominals|country=GBR|CBE|FRS}}<ref name="frs">{{Cite journal | last1 = Chory | first1 = J. | last2 = Casey | first2 = R. | doi = 10.1098/rsbm.2010.0014  | doi-access = free| title = Christopher John Lamb CBE. 19 March 1950 -- 21 August 2009 | journal = [[Biographical Memoirs of Fellows of the Royal Society]] | volume = 56 | pages = 189–213 | year = 2010 | s2cid = 85016599 }}</ref> (19 March 1950 – 21 August 2009) was a [[Professor]] of [[Botany|Plant Biology]] at the [[University of East Anglia]] and director of the [[John Innes Centre]].<ref name="Bevan"/><ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/news/obituaries/science-obituaries/6309097/Professor-Chris-Lamb.html |title=Professor Chris Lamb obituary in the Telegraph |work= The Daily Telegraph|accessdate=2011-08-03 |location=London |date=12 October 2009}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.jic.ac.uk/staff/chris-lamb/|title=Professor Chris Lamb at the John Innes Centre|accessdate=2011-08-03|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111025155112/http://www.jic.ac.uk/staff/chris-lamb/|archive-date=25 October 2011|url-status=dead}}</ref>

His field of study was plant–pathogen interactions, and he made many contributions to the understanding of [[plant pathology]].<ref name="Dixon">{{cite journal |last1=Dixon |first1=Richard A. |title=Chris Lamb: A Visionary Leader in Plant Science |journal=Annual Review of Phytopathology |date=8 September 2011 |volume=49 |issue=1 |pages=31–45 |doi=10.1146/annurev-phyto-072910-095224 |pmid=21838573 |language=en |issn=0066-4286|doi-access=free }}</ref>

==Education==
Lamb graduated from [[Fitzwilliam College, Cambridge]], with a [[Bachelor of Arts]] degree in [[Natural Sciences (Cambridge)|natural sciences]] with first class honours in 1972, which was followed by a [[PhD]] in plant [[biochemistry]] in 1976, also from Cambridge.<ref name="frs"/><ref name="Bevan">{{cite news |last1=Bevan |first1=Mike |title=Chris Lamb |url=https://www.theguardian.com/science/2009/aug/31/chris-lamb-obituary |work=The Guardian |date=31 August 2009}}</ref><ref name="Dixon"/>

==Career and research==
From 1975 to 1982 he worked at the [[University of Oxford]], first as an [[Imperial Chemical Industries|ICI]] Research Fellow in the School of Botany,<ref name="Dixon"/> then as a Browne Research Fellow at [[The Queen's College, Oxford|The Queen's College]].<ref name="frs"/> In 1982 he moved to the [[Salk Institute for Biological Studies]] in [[La Jolla]], [[California]] where he was director of the plant biology laboratory until 1998. In 1999 he returned to the United Kingdom, first at the [[University of Edinburgh]] where he was Regius Professor of Plant Science then at the [[University of East Anglia]] where he was a Professor and director of the [[John Innes Centre]].<ref name="Dixon"/><ref name="frs"/>
